subject: Marketplace listing: policy & branding gap analysis for upcoming co-sell
messages:
From: Sally Chen <sally.chen@partnercloud.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-05-22T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: Quick ask: marketplace listing policy checks for our co-sell

Hi Vanessa,

Thanks again for the demo last week — team was excited about the latency controls and dedicated routing. We're preparing the listing for AWS Marketplace and want to make sure there are no policy or branding items that could block our co-sell kickoff. Two specific asks: 

1) Are there any Redwood branding or claim restrictions we should avoid (e.g., "enterprise-grade SLA" type language) when listing under PartnerCloud?
2) Can you share any existing compliance artifacts (SOC 2 summary, data retention statements) to attach to the listing?

If easier, we can jump on a short call this week. Ideally want a go/no-go to meet PartnerCloud's launch window (first week of June).

Thanks,
Sally
Sally Chen
Partnerships Lead, PartnerCloud

--
Attachment: none

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Sally Chen <sally.chen@partnercloud.com>
Cc: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-05-22T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Quick ask: marketplace listing policy checks for our co-sell

Hi Sally — great to hear. Short answers up front:

- Branding/claims: avoid absolute uptime/SLA claims that aren't backed by marketplace-managed SLAs. We can say "SLA-backed options available" or reference our Dedicated offering and SLA tiers rather than a hard percent in the listing.
- Compliance artifacts: we have an SOC 2 summary and a short security FAQ we can surface.

I'm looping in Sergio (partnerships) for the marketplace checklist and Laura (marketing) for the listing copy. David from legal if we need any quick redlines.

If you can share PartnerCloud's marketplace checklist, we'll run a gap analysis and return a marked-up draft by Friday. Otherwise we'll apply our internal checklist and highlight any ask items. Call is fine — I have open slots Thursday 10-11am PT.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Head of Partnerships, Redwood Inference

--
Attachment: none

From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Sally Chen <sally.chen@partnercloud.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-05-23T08:30:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Quick ask: marketplace listing policy checks for our co-sell

Thanks Vanessa — attaching our working checklist (Excel). I did a quick pass against the preliminary PartnerCloud criteria Sally sent and flagged three likely friction points:

- Support SLA language: PartnerCloud requires a published support SLA on the listing. We currently publish tier descriptions but not a single customer-facing SLA percentage.
- Branding: PartnerCloud's guideline forbids partner claims like "zero-downtime" or "guaranteed 99.999%" unless the marketplace operator provides that SLA.
- Trial & billing descriptions: need to align billing flow with PartnerCloud's metering schema or the listing will fail validation.

Action items I've penciled in on the checklist:
- Draft a short public-facing SLA blurb that maps to our Dedicated offering but defers to PartnerCloud/AWS terms as required.
- Replace comparative superlatives ("best", "fastest") with feature-focused language and benchmark statements referencing our docs.
- Coordinate billing SDK mapping with engineering (I can loop Rishi if needed).

Attached: AWS_marketplace_checklist_v1.xlsx (workbook, checklist tab + notes).

Sergio
Director, Partnerships
Redwood Inference

--
Attachment: AWS_marketplace_checklist_v1.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)

From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Sally Chen <sally.chen@partnercloud.com>
Date: 2025-05-26T14:15:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Quick ask: marketplace listing policy checks for our co-sell

Folks — read the checklist. High-level legal guidance:

1) Reword SLA/uptime mentions. We should avoid fixed uptime % claims in the public listing. Suggested language: "Support plans available with contractual SLAs for Dedicated deployments; see our support page for details. Subject to marketplace terms."
2) Data handling & retention: include a short paragraph: "Customer data is processed per contract; we support region-specific data residency in Dedicated/Private deployments." Do not call out specific retention periods unless they are contractually guaranteed.
3) Trademark/branding: do not imply PartnerCloud endorsement beyond standard partner badges. Remove any claim like "PartnerCloud-certified" unless we complete their certification program.

I've drafted redlines in the attached doc; these are suggested changes to the listing copy and the proposed support blurb. If PartnerCloud insists on a single SLA field, we can provide a link to a hosted SLA page and a statement that contractual SLAs are available under customer agreements.

Next steps: Vanessa — approve redlines? Sergio — once we finalize, marketing to push the copy to the Seller Central draft URL. Laura, please coordinate updated screenshots that remove any disallowed comparative claims.

David Kim
General Counsel, Redwood Inference

--
Attachment: listing_terms_redline.docx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document)

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Sally Chen <sally.chen@partnercloud.com>, AWS Marketplace Compliance <aws-marketplace-compliance@amazon.com>
Cc: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-05-28T16:04:00-07:00
Subject: Final: listing copy + next steps for PartnerCloud co-sell

Sally / AWS compliance team — thanks for the patience. Summary of where we landed after an internal review: 

- Branding/claims: removed superlatives and any absolute uptime percentages. We now use the phrase: "Support plans available with contractual SLAs for Dedicated deployments; see support.redwood.com for details. Subject to marketplace terms."
- Compliance artifacts: attached our SOC 2 summary and security FAQ (I will upload to the Seller Central draft after we agree on copy).
- Billing/trial flow: Sergio will coordinate with PartnerCloud engineering to map metering fields (Rishi from engineering will be looped on the next thread).

Requested approvals / immediate asks: 
1) Sally — can PartnerCloud accept the revised SLA blurb above in the listing's SLA field, with a link to our hosted SLA?
2) AWS Compliance — quick confirmation that the updated language avoids policy rejection (cc'd). If there are any required phrasing or link formatting constraints, please flag them.
3) Marketing (Laura) & Legal (David) — final signoff on copy and screenshot assets.

I'll upload the draft to Seller Central here: https://sellercentral.amazon.com/listing/draft/REDWOOD-2025-05 (private until approved). Also sharing the DocuSign for the partner co-sell addendum if PartnerCloud is ready: https://www.docusign.com/en/documents/signature-request/abc123

Timeline: if we get approvals by EOD Friday 2025-05-30, we can publish during the PartnerCloud launch window.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Head of Partnerships, Redwood Inference
